knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given a Description

question.:question/problem:
Given that $f(x)={x}^{2}+3,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-2,2)$
- $x\in [0,\infty)$
- $x\in (-\infty,0]$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)={x}^{2}+3$ can be obtained in the following way:

- Take the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

- Translate it by $3$ units up to get $f(x)={x}^{2}+3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124474/plots/e636dc199bd92ad4996398cc664306d1ad1bfcbe6b600bbc8da5164fbe149fc1-0.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-2,2).$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124474/plots/e636dc199bd92ad4996398cc664306d1ad1bfcbe6b600bbc8da5164fbe149fc1-1.png)

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the intervals $x\in [0,\infty)$ and  $x\in (-\infty,0].$ On these intervals, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186124474/plots/e636dc199bd92ad4996398cc664306d1ad1bfcbe6b600bbc8da5164fbe149fc1-2.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".

question.:question/problem:
Given that $f(x)=|x-5|+3,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

III. - $x\in (-\infty,6]$

The graph of the function $f(x)=|x-5|+3$ can be obtained in the following way:

- Take the curve $y=|x|.$

- Translate it by $5$ units to the right,  to get $y=|x-5|.$

- Finally, translate $y=|x-5|$ by $3$ units up to get $f(x)=|x-5|+3.$

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty,4).$  Indeed, on this interval, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on any of the intervals $x\in (2,\infty)$  and $(-\infty,6].$ On each of these intervals, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

question.:question/problem:
Given that $f(x)=(x-2)^{2}+3,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

I. $x\in (2,\infty)$

II. $x\in (1,3]$

III. $x\in (2,4]$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it is one-to-one on that interval.

The vertex occurs at $x=2$. On either side of this vertex, the function is strictly monotone. Including the vertex as an endpoint does not create a repeated output. An interval containing points on both sides is not one-to-one: inputs equally far from the vertex have the same output.

- Interval I, $(2,\infty)$, lies on one side of the vertex, since $2\ge 2$. It is therefore invertible.

- Interval II, $(1,3]$, contains the distinct inputs $\frac{3}{2}$ and $\frac{5}{2}$, both with output $\frac{13}{4}$. It is therefore not invertible.

- Interval III, $(2,4]$, lies on one side of the vertex, since $2\ge 2$. It is therefore invertible.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
